project: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: Dancing with the SARs
phase: Phase 7B.1: Tree Explainability Mathematical Verification & Random Forest Model Integrity Audit

task_a_random_forest_architecture.split_criterion: Vectorized Gini impurity gain (10 linear candidate thresholds)
task_a_random_forest_architecture.ensemble_aggregation: Soft voting across all 40 independent trees

task_b_oob_terminology.correction: Model evaluation on test set (N=6,124) is held-out ensemble soft voting, not out-of-bag prediction.
task_b_oob_terminology.true_oob_characteristics: True OOB evaluates only bootstrap-omitted trees per sample (mean 18.89 trees on training set).

task_c_shapley_mathematical_verification.mathematical_distinction: Saabas tree-path attribution decomposes probabilities along the single observed path (telescoping sum), satisfying additivity. However, it is path-dependent and violates Shapley symmetry. Terminology downgraded to Pure-NumPy Tree-Path Attribution (Saabas Formulation).

task_d_feature_redundancy.credit_splitting_mitigation: Grouped Polarization Attribution aggregates both into a unified 10.67% attribution block.

task_f_probability_calibration.uncertainty_interpretation: abs(P - 0.5) is a decision margin / uncertainty proxy; NOT calibrated Bayesian confidence.

task_g_confusion_matrix_reconciliation.epistemological_correction: Specular scattering on moist char sands is a scientifically supported physical hypothesis, not an in-situ proven causal fact.

task_h_deterministic_baseline_thresholds.scientific_conclusion: Adaptive Otsu baseline derived in Phase 3A reflects seasonal hydrological shifts; static heuristic is overly conservative.
